subject: maths
question: A covered a distance of 240 km at a certain speed. Had his speed been 8 km/h less, then the time taken would have been one hour more for covering the same distance. How much time (in hours) will he take to cover a distance of 480 km at his original speed?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct formula for speed: Distance = [Product of speeds ÷ Difference in speeds] × Difference in time.

240 = [v × (v − 8) ÷ 8] × 1

v × (v − 8) = 1920 ⇒ By factorizing: 48 × 40 = 1920 ⇒ v = 48 km/h.

Time for 480 km = Distance ÷ Original Speed = 480 ÷ 48 = 10 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance₁ = 240 km, Distance₂ = 480 km, Time difference = 1 hour, Speed reduction = 8 km/h.

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/038c0065511de9d9a04d0dcf22c26f71a7650ce327b86a3ec36306b50b393230.png] 

Let the original speed be v km/h.

⇒ 240/(v − 8) − 240/v = 1

⇒ 240 [ (v − (v − 8)) ÷ (v(v − 8)) ] = 1

⇒ 240 × [ 8 ÷ (v² − 8v) ] = 1

⇒ 1920 = v² − 8v

⇒ v² − 8v − 1920 = 0

⇒ v² − 48v + 40v − 1920 = 0

⇒ (v − 48)(v + 40) = 0

⇒ v = 48 km/h (speed cannot be negative)

⇒ Required time for 480 km = 480 ÷ 48

⇒ Time = 10 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed and Time Relationship

When distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (s ∝ 1/t). If speed decreases by a factor, time increases by the inverse of that factor.

Average Speed for Constant Distance

If a journey is covered at speed 'a' and returned at speed 'b', the average speed is given by [2 × a × b ÷ (a + b)].

Speed-Time Variance Formula

For a fixed distance D, if speed changes from v₁ to v₂ resulting in time change Δt, then D = [v₁ × v₂ ÷ |v₁ − v₂|] × Δt.</p
